Subject: Final adjudication: OKR evidence, contested marks, and QBR comms

Team —

Attached is my proposed final scoring sheet for Q1 (file: 2027Q1_OKR_scores_proposal.csv) and the compressed evidence bundle (Q1_evidence_pack.zip). I tried to keep adjudication minimal where evidence is clear; there are three items I flagged as "contested" with short notes in the CSV:

- Objective A (Infra): delivery % bumped to 88% from 92% — rationale: test coverage gaps + post-release latency regs (see evidence/infra/latency_postmortem.md).
- Objective B (Serving): adoption metric revised down; instrumentation shows discrepancy between prod and canary (evidence/serving/telemetry-snapshots/).
- Objective C (Platform): recommended partial credit for cross-org enablement; outreach logs show limited uptake from two key partners.

Ask: please review the three contested rows and reply with either an explicit acceptance or a short counter-argument by EOD. I will consolidate and produce a one-paragraph narrative per objective for the QBR pack.

Also attached is a draft QBR communication template (QBR_comm_template_v2.docx) — we need to finalize the executive narrative and the 3-slide ask deck by Wednesday so GTM has time to prep.

If you accept my adjudication without comment, I'll lock the scores and push the narrative to the shared Drive link below. If you disagree, flag the exact evidence you want included.

Thanks,

--
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2027Q1_OKR_scores_proposal.csv (text/csv), Q1_evidence_pack.zip (zip), QBR_comm_template_v2.docx (application/vnd-openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks Ben — reviewed quickly and a few quick points:

1) Objective A: I accept the lowered delivery % but want the narrative to call out remediation steps (test backfill plan + ETA). Evidence in the pack is sufficient; no change to score but will add remediation bullet.

2) Objective B: I don’t accept the score cut as-is. The telemetry snapshot you reference shows different sampling windows; the production window (Feb 28–Mar 6) aligns with the rollout exposure. I propose we keep the original banding but note the sampling caveat in the narrative.

3) Objective C: agree with partial credit. However, Marissa — can you confirm partner outreach cadence? If we have two additional meetings scheduled in April (not yet in the evidence pack), I[0m'd recommend bumping to 60% rather than the proposed 50%.

I can draft objective-level bullets for the QBR narrative after we lock the scores.

-Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final adjudication: OKR evidence, contested marks, and QBR comms

Laura, Ben — thanks for the quick review.

A few notes from the leadership lens:

- On Objective B (Serving), I side with a compromise. The instrumentation mismatch is real but the user-facing impact was limited. Let's keep the original banding (as Laura suggests) but append an explicit mitigation line in the narrative and a 30-day telemetry check-in (owner: SRE). That preserves fairness without overstating progress.

- For Objective A remediation bullets: make sure the remediation ETA is prescriptive — weekly milestones, owners, and measurable signals. We should avoid vague "backfill tests" language.

- On communication: the executive QBR slide should have exactly two asks: (1) a short exception/credit ask for the infra incident remediation budget, and (2) a resource ask for an additional SRE headcount that maps to the 30-day telemetry check. Keep revenue/ops asks separate.

Ben — please incorporate the compromise on Objective B and add the two-line mitigation plan for Objective A. Marissa — if you confirm the April partner meetings in thread, Ben will use that to adjust Objective C.

I'd prefer we close this thread by 3:30pm PT so GTM can start slide prep.

–Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Engineering, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
